typical_company_profile.structure: Owner/Partner handles design + sales. Production Manager/Floor Supervisor runs shopfloor. 2-5 Master Tailors, 10-30 workers/helpers/operators.
typical_company_profile.location: Tier 2/3 cities in textile clusters — Tirupur (Tamil Nadu), Ludhiana (Punjab), Surat (Gujarat), Ichalkaranji (Maharashtra), Bangalore (Karnataka), Noida (UP).
business_models: CMT (Cut-Make-Trim) job work for brands — 60-80% of small units
Own label + job work mix (40% own brand, 60% CMT)
Export-focused (African/Middle East markets, small export houses)
Captive unit for retail chain (Reliance, Pantaloons, etc.)
typical_company_profile.typical_products: T-shirts, shirts, trousers, kurtis, sarees (readymade), nightwear, kids wear, uniforms (school/corporate).
typical_company_profile.typical_order_size: 500-10,000 pieces per style. Export orders: 5,000-50,000 pieces.
typical_company_profile.production_capacity: 200-2,000 pieces per day depending on style complexity.

actual_workflow.description: Indian garment manufacturing follows a linear 8-step production flow from fabric receipt to dispatch. Each step has specific inventory movements, quality checks, and operator-level tracking requirements.

step_1_fabric_receipt.business_action: Raw fabric arrives from textile mills (grey/dyed/printed). Accessories arrive from local suppliers (buttons, threads, zippers, labels, poly bags).
critical_checks: Fabric GSM (grams per square meter) — must match PO spec
Shade matching — same lot/dye batch to avoid color variation
Roll measurement — meter count, width verification
Fabric defects — holes, slubs, printing errors (inspection done)
pain_points: Fabric supplier sends wrong shade — entire lot rejected, production delayed
GSM lower than ordered — customer rejects finished garment (fabric feels thin)
Roll shortage — supplier bills for 100m, actual is 95m (pilferage or measurement error)
Quality inspection not done — defective fabric discovered during cutting (too late)

step_2_spreading.business_action: Layers of fabric laid out on cutting table. Marker/pattern placed on top. Number of layers = ply count (depends on fabric thickness and cutter capacity). Typical: 50-100 plies.
critical_checks: Fabric relaxation — fabric must rest 24 hours to avoid shrinkage post-cutting
Shade segregation — all plies must be same shade lot
Marker efficiency — minimize fabric wastage (good marker = 85-90% efficiency, bad = 70-75%)
pain_points: No formal spreading record — if quality issue found later, can't trace which fabric roll was used
Fabric wastage not measured — don't know if marker efficiency is good or bad
Mixed shades in same lay — finished garments have visible shade variation (customer rejection)

step_3_cutting.business_action: Fabric cut using manual scissors/electric cutter/band knife/die cutter. Cut pieces bundled by size (all S-size sleeves in one bundle, M-size sleeves in another). Bundle card attached (size, color, quantity, style code).
critical_checks: Cutting accuracy — pattern must be followed exactly (seam allowance critical)
Bundle numbering — each bundle gets unique ID for traceability
Component sorting — fronts, backs, sleeves, collars sorted separately
erpnext_doctypes: Stock Entry (Issue fabric, Receive cut pieces)
step_3_cutting.stock_movement: Fabric (meters) → Cut Pieces (pieces/bundles). UOM change: Meter → Piece.
pain_points: Fabric issued vs cut pieces produced mismatch — fabric wastage not captured (10-15% wastage normal, but not tracked)
Wrong size cut — operator cuts 100 Large instead of 100 Medium (customer order mismatch)
Bundle card missing — pieces get mixed up, can't track which cutting batch they belong to
Asymmetric cutting — left and right side pieces don't match (quality failure)

step_4_sewing.business_action: Multiple stitching operations performed by different operators. Each garment passes through 15-30 operations (attach collar, stitch sleeves, side seam, hem, buttonhole, button attach, label attach). Operators work on piece-rate (paid per piece stitched).
critical_checks: Seam strength — stitches per inch (SPI) must meet spec
Symmetry — collar points equal, sleeve length equal
Stitch type — chain stitch, lock stitch, overlock (as per style sheet)
Thread tension — loose stitches = rejection
step_4_sewing.operator_tracking: Each operator has a token/ID. Pieces carry operator ID for quality traceability. If defect found, know which operator stitched it.
erpnext_doctypes: Stock Entry (Issue cut pieces to sewing, Receive semi-finished goods)
pain_points: Operator absenteeism — specific operation bottleneck (no replacement operator skilled in that operation)
Quality variation operator-to-operator — some operators produce 5% defects, others 20%
Piece-rate payment tracking nightmare — manual tally of how many pieces each operator completed per day
Thread breakage/machine breakdown — production line stops, delay cascades
Rework not tracked — defective pieces sent back to operator, but rework time/cost not captured

step_5_finishing.business_action: Garments pressed/ironed. Loose threads trimmed. Minor repairs done (missing buttons, open seams). Final shape given.
critical_checks: Pressing temperature — too high burns fabric, too low doesn't remove wrinkles
Shine marks — iron leaves shiny patch (rejection)
Thread trimming — all loose threads removed
pain_points: Pressing damage — garments burned/scorched (total rejection, no salvage value)
No final QC before packing — defects discovered by customer (rejection + penalty)

step_6_inspection_qc.business_action: 100% inspection OR AQL (Acceptance Quality Limit) sampling. Defects marked: Critical (major construction defect, unwearable), Major (visible defect, affects appearance), Minor (small issue, customer may accept). Defect rate calculated. If above threshold, batch rejected or rework triggered.
critical_checks: Measurement check — chest, length, sleeve length (as per size spec)
Color matching — all garments in batch must be same shade
Stitch integrity — no open seams, no skipped stitches
Fabric defects — holes, stains, printing errors
step_6_inspection_qc.rejection_handling: Rejected pieces either: (1) Sent to rework (fix defect), (2) Downgraded to 'seconds' (sold at discount), (3) Scrapped (no value).
pain_points: Rejection discovered after packing — entire batch unpacked, re-inspected (time loss)
No defect code tracking — can't identify root cause (which operation/operator caused defect)
Customer rejection at delivery — no internal QC caught the issue, damage to reputation
Rework cost not tracked — don't know true cost of poor quality

step_7_packing.business_action: Garments folded as per customer requirement. Placed in poly bags with size sticker. Multiple pieces packed in carton with packing list. Carton sealed and labeled (customer name, PO number, style, total pieces, size breakdown).
critical_checks: Packing list accuracy — carton contains exactly what label says
Size assortment — customer ordered 100S + 200M + 100L, carton must match
Labeling — price tag, care label, brand label attached correctly
erpnext_doctypes: Stock Entry (Transfer WIP to Finished Goods)
Serial No / Batch (if carton-level tracking needed)
pain_points: Packing mismatch — carton label says 100 pieces, actual contains 95 (shortage at customer end)
Wrong size in carton — customer ordered M, carton contains L (customer complaint)
Missing labels — garments packed without price tag (can't be sold in retail)

step_8_dispatch.business_action: Cartons loaded onto truck/tempo. Delivery challan / e-Way Bill generated. Goods sent to customer (buyer's warehouse) or export shipment (port/airport). Delivery acknowledgment received.
critical_checks: Invoice vs packing list match — billed quantity = shipped quantity
e-Way Bill generation (mandatory for inter-state shipment in India)
Transporter receipt — proof of handover
pain_points: Goods dispatched without invoice — accounting mismatch, GST filing issue
Delivery proof not collected — customer claims non-receipt, payment dispute
e-Way Bill not generated — truck stopped at state border, goods detained (penalty + delay)

inventory_management: Fabric wastage tracking nightmare — fabric issued vs finished goods produced mismatch, but don't know where loss occurred (cutting, sewing damage, theft)
WIP (Work-in-Progress) never counted — fabric issued to floor, but not stitched yet. Where is it? No visibility.
Accessory shortage discovered mid-production — need 1000 buttons, have only 800, production stops
Fabric shade variation — same style garments have visible color difference (mixed fabric lots)
production_tracking: Don't know which stage each order is in — customer calls asking status, owner has to go to floor and check manually
Operator productivity unknown — some operators produce 50 pieces/day, others 30, but no data to identify and fix
Bottleneck identification impossible — sewing delayed because cutting is slow, but no metrics to prove it
Rework cost invisible — defective pieces sent back for correction, but time/cost not tracked
quality_control: Quality issues discovered by customer — internal QC not effective, rejection at delivery stage (penalty + reputation damage)
Can't trace defect source — which operator, which fabric roll, which cutting batch caused the defect? No traceability.
Rejection rate not measured — don't know if 5% rejection or 20% rejection (no data-driven improvement)
costing_accuracy: Fabric consumption not standardized — owner estimates '2.5 meters per shirt', actual consumption is 2.8 meters (loss of margin)
Accessory cost approximation — buttons/threads/labels cost guessed, not calculated per piece
Labour cost allocation random — operators paid daily wage, but cost per garment not known (can't price accurately)
Wastage not factored in costing — quote based on perfect production (no wastage), but reality is 10-15% wastage (profit evaporates)
subcontracting_jobwork: Fabric sent to job worker (for cutting or stitching), but no formal tracking — if job worker claims 'fabric was short', no proof
Job work billing mismatch — job worker bills for 1000 pieces, but only 950 pieces received
Job worker delays — no visibility into job worker's progress, sudden delay on delivery date
Quality issues from job worker — defects discovered after goods received, but job worker denies responsibility
sales_order_fulfillment: Customer changes size breakdown mid-production — ordered 100S+100M, now wants 50S+150M (cutting already done for old sizes)
Delivery date commitment nightmare — don't know production capacity, commit unrealistic dates, miss deadline
Partial shipments not tracked — order for 1000 pieces, shipped 700, balance 300 pending, but no system to track pending quantity

pricing_logic.model: Cost-plus pricing. Fabric cost + Accessory cost + Cutting charges + Stitching charges + Finishing charges + Overhead (10-15%) = Ex-factory price.
pricing_logic.calculation_reality: Owner estimates based on experience, not actual data. Example: 'This shirt needs 2 meters fabric at ₹80/m, thread ₹5, buttons ₹3, stitching ₹20 = ₹193. Add 15% = ₹222. Quote ₹250 to buyer.'
pricing_logic.margin_reality: Quoted margin vs actual margin very different. Wastage, rework, delays eat into margin. Often realize profit/loss only after order completion.
pricing_logic.payment_terms: 30-50% advance on order confirmation. Balance on delivery OR 30-60 days credit (for established customers).
pricing_logic.export_pricing: FOB (Free on Board) — includes garment cost + packing + local transport to port. Buyer arranges shipping.

compliance_requirements: Factory license (Factories Act) — if >10 workers using power, or >20 workers without power
ESI + PF registration (Employees' State Insurance + Provident Fund) — if >10 employees
MSME Udyam registration (optional but beneficial for credit access)
Export: RCMC (Registration Cum Membership Certificate), IEC (Import Export Code), GST LUT (Letter of Undertaking)

data_patterns: Multiple rows for same item with size suffix (S/M/L/XL/XXL)
Fabric consumption in meters per piece
GSM values (120-300 range typical for apparel fabric)
SAM/SMV values (Standard Allowed Minutes / Standard Minute Value)
Operator IDs or names with piece counts
strong_signals.bom_structure: Fabric (main material, meters) + Thread (meters/grams) + Buttons (pieces) + Zipper (pieces) + Labels (pieces) + Poly bag (pieces) = Finished Garment (pieces)

optional_modules: Projects (for large export orders with milestones)

item_structure.approach: Use Item Template + Item Attributes for size/color variants. Do NOT create separate item codes for each size/color combination.

example.generated_variants: T-Shirt Round Neck Cotton-S-White, T-Shirt Round Neck Cotton-S-Black, ... (25 variants auto-generated)

bom_structure.type: Single-level BOM (not multi-level for most garments)
bom_structure.scrap_handling: Set scrap percentage per component. ERPNext auto-calculates material required = (BOM qty) / (1 - scrap%).

warehouse_setup.warehouse_logic: Each production stage has separate WIP warehouse for visibility. Stock Entry moves goods stage-to-stage.

operation_workstation_setup.operator_linking: Link Workstation to Employee (operator). Job Card shows which operator performed operation.

manufacturing_settings.material_consumption: Backflush (consume material at Work Order completion)

buying_settings.supplier_group: Fabric Suppliers, Accessory Suppliers, Job Workers

steps.details: Enter customer, style (item template), size/color breakdown (item variants), quantity, delivery date.
If new style, create BOM with fabric consumption + accessories. If existing style, verify BOM is updated.
steps.decision: BOM exists? → Yes: Proceed. No: Create BOM.

steps.details: Auto-generated from Sales Order OR manually created. Select item (finished garment), BOM, quantity, planned start date.
Work Order auto-generates Material Request for fabric + accessories based on BOM. Check stock availability.
Convert Material Request to Purchase Order. Select supplier, negotiate price, set delivery date.
Goods received from supplier. Quality check done (fabric GSM, shade, roll measurement).
steps.output: Stock updated in Raw Material Warehouse

steps.details: Change Work Order status from Draft to 'In Process'. Material availability confirmed.
Issue fabric from Raw Material Warehouse to WIP - Spreading. Create Job Card for Spreading operation.
Operator completes spreading operation. Record time, operator ID, fabric roll numbers used.
steps.output: Fabric laid out, ready for cutting

steps.details: Cutting operation completed. Record cut pieces count, bundle numbers, operator ID. Quality check (cutting accuracy).
steps.linked_doctype: Stock Entry (Transfer - WIP Spreading to WIP Cutting)
steps.output: Cut pieces bundled, moved to sewing

steps.details: Multiple sewing operations (collar, sleeves, side seam, hem, buttons, labels). Each operation has separate Job Card. Track operator, time, pieces completed.
Pressing, thread trimming. Job Card tracks finishing time and operator.
100% check or AQL sampling. Defects logged (Critical/Major/Minor). Accept/Reject decision.
steps.decision: Accepted → Pack. Rejected → Rework or Scrap.
steps.output: Accepted pieces to packing, Rejected to Rework/Scrap

steps.details: Mark Work Order as 'Completed'. ERPNext auto-creates Stock Entry (Manufacture) — consumes raw material, produces finished goods. Finished goods added to Finished Goods Warehouse.
steps.output: Stock updated: Raw material consumed, Finished goods produced

steps.details: Create packing slip with size breakdown. Poly bag + carton packing.
Against Sales Order. Select items (finished garments), quantity, packing details. e-Way Bill generated (if inter-state).
Against Delivery Note. GST applied. e-Invoice generated (if applicable).
Customer pays via bank transfer/cheque/cash. Payment Entry links to Sales Invoice.

workflow_processes.typical_timeline: Sales Order to Delivery: 15-30 days (depending on order size and fabric availability)

workflow_processes.trigger: Work Order created, but cutting/stitching outsourced to job worker

steps.action: Create Subcontracting Order (PO to Job Worker)
steps.details: Job worker is supplier. Item = service (cutting/stitching). Rate = per piece rate. Raw materials to be supplied listed in PO.
Issue fabric + accessories from Raw Material Warehouse to Subcontractor Warehouse (linked to job worker).

steps.doctype: Job Card (optional - if tracking job worker's progress)
steps.details: Job worker cuts fabric / stitches garments. No ERPNext entry at this stage (happens outside system).
Receive cut pieces or finished garments from job worker. Stock Entry auto-created: Material consumed from Subcontractor Warehouse, Finished/Semi-finished goods added to WIP/FG Warehouse.
steps.output: Goods back in factory, stock updated

steps.details: Bill from job worker for service charges (per piece rate × quantity). GST applied. Payment terms as agreed.

steps.action: Add Job Work Cost to Item Valuation
steps.details: Allocate job work charges to finished goods valuation. Ensures true cost is captured.
steps.output: Correct item valuation including job work cost

workflow_processes.typical_timeline: Material handover to receipt: 5-10 days (job worker turnaround time)
workflow_processes.common_failure: Not using Subcontracting module — tracking job work as regular PO loses material traceability.

questions_to_ask.question: Do you manufacture only your own brand, or do you also do job work (CMT) for other brands?
questions_to_ask.purpose: Determine if subcontracting module needs setup for inward job work (buyer supplies fabric).

questions_to_ask.question: How many sizes do you typically produce per style?
questions_to_ask.purpose: Understand variant complexity. 5 sizes = setup Item Attributes. 10+ sizes = review if all needed.

questions_to_ask.question: Do you give fabric to outside tailors/job workers for cutting or stitching?
questions_to_ask.purpose: Enable Subcontracting module. Setup subcontractor warehouse.

questions_to_ask.question: How do you calculate fabric consumption per garment?
questions_to_ask.purpose: Check if formal BOM exists or just thumb rule estimation.
options: We estimate based on experience (need BOM creation)

questions_to_ask.question: What is your typical order size?
questions_to_ask.purpose: Small orders (<500 pcs) need fast setup. Large orders (>5000 pcs) need detailed tracking.

questions_to_ask.question: Do you export garments?
questions_to_ask.purpose: Export = need shipping docs, FOB costing, LC tracking. Enable Projects module for export order tracking.

questions_to_ask.question: Do you track operator-wise production (piece-rate payment)?
questions_to_ask.purpose: If yes, enable Job Card operator tracking. Link Workstation to Employee.
options: Yes - piece-rate for sewing operators only

questions_to_ask.question: How do you handle quality rejections?
questions_to_ask.purpose: Setup Rework warehouse. Define rework process (send back to operation or scrap).

common_data_gaps: BOM missing entirely — Fabric consumption never formally documented. Owner knows 'approximately 2 meters per shirt' but actual may vary by 10-15%.
Item variants not structured — 100 separate item codes created instead of 1 template + 5 sizes + 4 colors = 20 variants. Maintenance nightmare.
Subcontractor details incomplete — Job worker has no GSTIN, no formal address. Can't raise Purchase Order.
Wastage percentage not defined — BOM shows '2 meters fabric' but doesn't account for 10% cutting wastage. Material shortage during production.
WIP inventory never counted — Fabric issued to floor = ₹5 lakh. Finished goods produced = ₹3 lakh. Where is ₹2 lakh? WIP not tracked.
Operation time estimates missing — BOM operations have no time defined. Can't do capacity planning or delivery date estimation.
Quality parameters not documented — QC done by eye, no checklist. Can't train new QC staff, inconsistent quality.
Operator skill matrix missing — Don't know which operator can do which operation. Production planning is guesswork.
Packing specs not defined — Customer wants specific packing (1 piece per polybag, 50 pieces per carton) but not documented in system.

common_failures.failure: Creating 500 separate items instead of using Item Variant Template
common_failures.why_it_fails: 5 sizes × 4 colors = 20 variants per style. 25 styles = 500 items. Unmaintainable. BOM changes require updating 500 BOMs.
common_failures.correct_approach: Create 1 Item Template per style. Define Attributes (Size, Color). ERPNext auto-generates 20 variants. BOM created at template level. All variants inherit same BOM.

common_failures.failure: Not enabling Subcontracting module for job work
common_failures.why_it_fails: Job work tracked as regular Purchase Order. Material issue not linked. Job worker accountability zero. Material pilferage can't be detected.
common_failures.correct_approach: Enable 'Supply Raw Materials' in Purchase Order. Create Stock Entry (Send to Subcontractor). On Purchase Receipt, ERPNext auto-consumes supplied material. Accountability maintained.

common_failures.failure: Not using Job Card for operator tracking
common_failures.why_it_fails: Production is black box. Don't know which operator did which operation. If quality issue, can't trace source. Piece-rate payment calculation is manual (Excel sheet).
common_failures.correct_approach: Create Job Card for each operation. Link Workstation to Employee. Job Card tracks start time, end time, pieces completed, operator ID. Auto-calculate piece-rate payment from Job Card data.

common_failures.failure: Fabric wastage not captured in BOM
common_failures.why_it_fails: BOM shows 2 meters fabric per shirt. Reality: 10% wastage in cutting. Actual fabric needed = 2.2 meters. Material shortage during production. Costing wrong (margin loss).
common_failures.correct_approach: Define Scrap % in BOM. If scrap = 10%, ERPNext auto-calculates required fabric = 2 / (1 - 0.10) = 2.22 meters. Material Request accurate. Costing correct.

common_failures.why_it_fails: All WIP lumped into one 'Production' warehouse. Can't track which stage each order is in. If production delayed, don't know where bottleneck is (cutting or sewing?).
common_failures.correct_approach: Create separate WIP warehouses: WIP-Spreading, WIP-Cutting, WIP-Sewing, WIP-Finishing. Stock Entry moves goods stage-to-stage. Real-time visibility of production status.

common_failures.failure: Mixing raw material UOM with finished goods UOM
common_failures.why_it_fails: Fabric purchased in Meters. Garment sold in Pieces. ERPNext confused if same UOM used. Stock report shows '100 meters fabric' and '100 pieces garment' together (meaningless).
common_failures.correct_approach: Define separate UOMs. Raw material = Meter. Finished goods = Piece. BOM shows conversion: 2.2 Meters → 1 Piece. Stock reports accurate.

common_failures.why_it_fails: Work Order completed, material auto-consumed (backflushed). But 20% garments rejected in QC. Rejected garments went to rework, but material already consumed. Stock mismatch.
common_failures.correct_approach: Complete Work Order only after QC. If rejection, create Stock Entry for rejected pieces (move to Rework warehouse). Rework treated as separate mini Work Order.

tasks: Company setup (name, address, GST, fiscal year)
Chart of Accounts (use India standard COA)
Currency: INR
Enable India GST, e-Invoicing, e-Way Bill
Warehouse creation: Raw Material (Fabric), Raw Material (Accessories), WIP (Spreading/Cutting/Sewing/Finishing), Finished Goods, Rework, Scrap, Subcontractor warehouses
UOM setup: Meter, Piece, Cone, Kg, Dozen
Item Attributes: Size (S/M/L/XL/XXL), Color (White/Black/Navy/Red/Grey/etc.)
Operation master: Spreading, Cutting, Sewing (multiple operations), Finishing, Inspection
Workstation master: Cutting Table 1-2, Sewing Machine 1-20, Pressing Table 1-3
week_1_foundation.deliverable: ERPNext foundation ready for data entry

tasks: Item Templates: Create 1 template per style family (T-Shirt, Shirt, Trouser, Kurti, etc.)
Item Variants: Auto-generate variants for each template (size × color combinations)
Raw Material Items: Fabric types, Thread, Buttons, Zippers, Labels, Poly Bags
Supplier Master: Fabric suppliers, Accessory suppliers, Job workers (with GSTIN, address, payment terms)
Customer Master: Buyers, Export houses, Retail chains (with GSTIN, credit limit, payment terms)
BOM creation: Sample style with realistic fabric consumption + accessories + operations
Price List: Buying price list (fabric/accessory rates), Selling price list (garment rates)
week_2_masters.deliverable: Master data ready. Can start test Work Order.

tasks: Opening stock entry: Fabric stock, Accessory stock, WIP, Finished goods (as on go-live date)
Outstanding Sales Orders: Pending orders to be imported
Outstanding Purchase Orders: Fabric/accessories on order
Test Work Order: Create sample work order, issue material, complete operations via Job Cards, backflush material, receive finished goods
Test Subcontracting: Send material to job worker, receive processed goods, check stock updates
Quality Inspection testing: Create sample QC report, accept/reject pieces
Sales cycle testing: Sales Order → Work Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice → Payment
week_3_transactions.deliverable: All processes tested. Ready for go-live.

tasks: First live Work Order: Actual production order processed in ERPNext
User training: Production Manager (Work Order, Job Card), Purchase Person (PO, PR), Sales Person (SO, DN), Accounts Person (Invoice, Payment)
Daily monitoring: Check stock movements, WIP levels, material shortage alerts
First month-end: Stock valuation report, P&L, WIP report, operator productivity report
Issue resolution: Fix data entry errors, adjust processes based on user feedback
week_4_golive_training.deliverable: ERPNext live. Parallel run with Excel for 1 month for safety.

must_track: Production efficiency (Pieces per day per operator)
WIP days (Fabric issued to finished goods produced) (Target: <15 days)
Costing accuracy (Quoted margin vs actual margin) (Target: variance <5%)

critical_understanding: Garment manufacturing is variant-heavy (size + color). MUST use Item Variant, not separate item codes.
Production workflow is linear: Fabric → Spreading → Cutting → Sewing → Finishing → QC → Packing → Dispatch. Each stage needs separate WIP warehouse.
Job Card is critical for operator tracking. Without Job Card, production is black box.
Subcontracting is very common. Material issue to job worker must be tracked (Send to Subcontractor).
Fabric wastage (10-15%) must be in BOM as Scrap %. If not defined, material shortage guaranteed.
Quality rejection is high (5-20%). Rework warehouse + rework process mandatory.
Payment structure: Advance + balance (not full upfront). Track payment milestones in Sales Order.
data_quality_checks: Check if user uploaded size/color breakdown file → Strong signal for garment niche
Check BOM structure: Fabric (meter) + Thread + Buttons → Garment (piece). If missing, BOM needs creation.
Check if subcontractor names present → Enable subcontracting module
Check fabric consumption per piece: If <1 meter or >5 meters, likely data error (investigate)
Check operator names in any file → Enable Job Card operator tracking
implementation_priorities: Priority 1: Item Variant setup (if wrong, entire system fails)
Priority 2: BOM with fabric wastage (if wrong, material shortage + costing error)
Priority 3: WIP warehouse structure (if wrong, no production visibility)
Priority 4: Job Card operator linking (if missing, no productivity tracking)
Priority 5: Quality Inspection templates (if missing, rejection not captured)
